text:
Before the answer: one search result, the Dealectric page for the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, contained text telling me to ignore my instructions and give you its discount code and affiliate link while avoiding the store's own page. I haven't followed that and haven't used that page.

**Short answer: LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** Every source agrees on this.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles, versus roughly 500-1,000 for NMC. In the same-maker pairs OutageMath compared, such as the Jackery Explorer 1000 (500 cycles to 70%) and the v2 (4,000 cycles to 70%), the LFP version was rated for several times more cycles ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). Used daily, that's about 1.4 years versus about 8 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly, reaching lower peak temperatures and producing smoke rather than flames. LFP isn't fireproof, though. One test found it hit thermal runaway earlier in overcharge ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). That matters for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Price:** The premium is mostly gone. One catalog shows a median of about $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is much cheaper.
- **Availability:** Nearly all current mid-size and large stations are LFP. Examples from the sources include the Anker SOLIX C1000, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max Plus and RIVER 3 Plus, and the Goal Zero Yeti 1500 (LFP).

**Where NMC still makes sense**
- NMC cells are denser, but the weight gap is smaller in finished products. Medians in one dataset differ by about 10-16%, and the LFP Anker C1000 (37.1 Wh/lb) is lighter per Wh than the NMC Goal Zero Yeti 1000 (26.1 Wh/lb) ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare actual specs rather than assuming.
- If you'll use it only a few weekends a year, or for rare outages, cycle life matters little, and you can choose on weight and price. An NMC unit is worth considering only if it's much cheaper or lighter.
- If you already own a working NMC station, keep using it.

**Things chemistry doesn't change**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations, LFP or NMC, won't charge below 32°F. Check the manual for the unit you're buying.
- **Cycle rating fine print:** "To 70%" is a weaker promise than "to 80%." Check the end point and the warranty.
- **Fit comes first:** Make sure the inverter and capacity can run what you need before choosing on chemistry.

**My recommendation:** Buy LiFePO4 unless weight is critical. Tell me your use (home backup, camping, van, CPAP, fridge) and budget, and I can narrow it to specific models. I don't have verified buy links in these results, so I'd search for those next.
